weekly_digest.narrative: 本周尚未结束（4/7 天）日均 208 条。合并 133 条、关闭 197 条。领域分布：推理 492、训练 234、方向 10、通用 96。热点主题：CUDA/Kernel (216)、GRPO/PPO (115)、Attention (103)。

focus: vLLM 的 CUDA/Kernel 模块本周将 GLM-5.3-Flash 的 decode 全路径融合至 CuTe/FlashInfer 专用 kernel，Hopper E2E 吞吐提升约 12%，是通用推理引擎首次做到模型级全定制。
SGLang Attention 模块为 RDNA3 新增 opt-in 后端并落地 cache-free prefill 上下文，Qwen3-VL 文本编码延迟削减 37–47%，多模态扩散 serving 可跳过 KV 调度直接跑模型层栈。
TensorRT-LLM CUDA/Kernel 模块交付 DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash 的 NVFP4 modeling_v2 手写目标（SM103/GB300），同时修复 KDA replay kernel 的 Triton 对齐特化，消除运行时重编译。
verl 的 GRPO/PPO 模块本周趋势下行，Rubin SM107 NVFP4 KV cache 被标记为不支持暴露了硬件矩阵与 DSA 路径的脱节；vLLM Quantization 模块上行，修复了融合层 packed_modules_mapping 在 FP8 量化下的对齐。

key_prs.why: 模型级 decode kernel 全融合首次落地通用推理引擎，Hopper 上所有 GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 用户直接受益，11.8–12% E2E 提升。
消除扩散路径中 Qwen3-VL 文本编码器的独立副本，37–47% 延迟削减直接惠及多模态 serving 与机器人后训练场景。
手写 NVFP4 目标意味着 GB300 上 DeepSeek-V4.1 从自动 codegen 转为手工优化，性能上限更高但后续维护成本显著上升。

items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: After #53249 the attention backends read the row width from the pool, but at every site: about 120 reads of (or ), and the page count recomputed about 14 times, including in backends that already stored it (FlashAttention keeps and recomputed it in graph captu…
items.body:
## Motivation

After #53249 the attention backends read the `req_to_token` row width from the pool, but at every site: about 120 reads of `req_to_token_pool.row_width` (or `req_to_token.shape[1]`), and the page count `(row_width + page_size - 1) // page_size` recomputed about 14 times, including in backends that already stored it (FlashAttention keeps `self.max_num_pages` and recomputed it in graph capture).

## Modifications

- Each attention backend derives its KV-table bounds once in `__init__`, from the pool:
  - `self.max_kv_len`: the longest KV a request can read, the pool's row width.

items.author: yeh-sudo

items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On Jetson Thor (SM110), vLLM's CUTLASS FP8 GEMMs lose about half their throughput once `M` passes a few thousand tokens, and become slower than torch's BF16 GEMM. This PR gives SM110 its own FP8 and blockwise FP8 `cutlass_scaled_mm` dispatch, tuned with `cutlass_profiler` on the Qwen3.8-27B projection shapes.

#41260 also added SM110 FP8 kernels, but was closed without any comments or benchmarks. #18778, #19566 and #20071 tuned the FP8 GEMMs for SM100 and did not cover SM110. The open PR #47149 also edits the `version_num` checks in `scaled_mm_entry.

## Motivation

For Inkling-2-Mini (#51926). Each DSpark draft step of Inkling-2-Mini adds a Markov bias over the whole vocabulary: a 201,024 x 256 BF16 head (about 103 MB) is read once per draft step, seven times per round. items.author: Autumn1998
items.summary: Adds end-to-end AngularMuOwn optimizer combining Adam row-scale updates with Muon angular steps via Newton–Schulz to MFSDP v2, including MCore integration and distributed checkpoints.
items.body:
## Goal

Support the AngularMuOwn optimizer ([Muown Implicitly Performs Angular Step-size Decay](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23637)) for Muon matrices under MFSDP v2, end to end in Megatron-LM: optimizer, MCore integration, and checkpoints.

## Background

AngularMuOwn writes each row as `W_i = g_i U_i`. Adam updates the signed row scales `g`; the unit directions `U` take a Muon step scaled by `lr * kappa_t` and are renormalized, with `kappa_t = (1 + c * max(0, t - t_w))^(-p)`. items.title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Fix GDN ReplaySSM losing the state update of a one-token prompt chunk
items.author: sansblues
items.summary: Flushes the ReplaySSM ring buffer when a single prompt token is processed in decode mode, preventing stale state from corrupting subsequent prefill chunks.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #70064. With ReplaySSM, a prompt token that runs as a decode only goes to the ring. If the prompt's next chunk is longer, the prefill path starts from the stale state and resets the ring, so that token's update is lost. This flushes the ring on such steps.

## Claims

- A prompt token that runs as a decode now flushes the ring, so the next prefill chunk starts from the exact state.
- Normal decoding is unchanged. The extra flushes only happen while a prompt is fed one token at a time.

## Validation

Tested at 69d3af837 on an RTX 3050 Ti under WSL2. The patch applies cleanly

items.title: [https://nvbugs/6928055][fix] Record streaming disagg requests before [DONE]
items.author: reasonsolo
items.summary: For streaming requests, most records can be lost: clients disconnect as soon as they receive, while the disaggregated record is appended only after the trailing performance-metrics event has been consumed. Under uvicorn's ASGI spec, Starlette cancels the strea…
items.body:
## Problem

With `perf_metrics_output_dir` set, the disaggregated server should write one JSONL record for every request. For streaming requests, most records can be lost: clients disconnect as soon as they receive `data: [DONE]`, while the disaggregated record is appended only after the trailing performance-metrics event has been consumed. Under uvicorn's ASGI spec, Starlette cancels the streaming response on that disconnect before `on_resp_done` or the middleware's final-body path runs.

This supersedes #20280, rebasing the fix onto current main and addressing its remaining review findings.

items.title: [Feat] hicache: Add an earliest_completion storage prefetch policy
items.author: ZeXi0308
items.summary: The static storage prefetch policies decide how long a request waits for its L3 read without looking at the reader or the GPU. In a burst of requests that resume from L3, keeps most of them waiting behind the single reader until their budgets end, while the GP…
items.body:
## Motivation

Closes #52823.

The static storage prefetch policies decide how long a request waits for its L3 read without looking at the reader or the GPU. In a burst of requests that resume from L3, `timeout` keeps most of them waiting behind the single reader until their budgets end, while the GPU has nothing to prefill. `best_effort` avoids that, but a request that arrives alone is prefilled even though its read would have finished first.

This PR adds an opt-in policy, `earliest_completion`, that makes the choice per L3 hit from two measured rates. The default stays `timeout`.

items.title: [Bugfix] Inkling 2: keep split-KV decode for large full-layer batches
items.author: Roshyoshi
items.summary: Fixes integer-division floor in plan_decode_attention that zeroed split-KV for large full-layer decode batches, restoring the split-KV kernel and doubling decode throughput on B300.
items.body:
## Overview

`plan_decode_attention` returns 0 ("use FA4") for full-layer decode and verify batches once `num_reqs * num_kv_heads > 6 * num_sms`, because both integer divisions floor to 0. This floors the plan at one split, so those batches stay on the split-KV decode kernel.

## Claims

- On a 148-SM B300 with 8 KV heads, decode and verify batches of more than 111 requests no longer fall back to FA4 on the full layers.
- Inkling-2-Mini on one B300, output tok/s with prompts cached:
  - draft off, 32K context, 128 requests: 1,560 -> 3,208
  - draft off, 8K context, 256 requests: 4,460 -> 7,6

items.title: [Fix] scheduler: Size the min-free-slots threshold to the admission cap
items.author: thanhhao98
items.summary: Fixes min-free-slots delayer threshold in the PP scheduler to respect the actual admission cap (pp_max_micro_batch_size) instead of max_running_requests, preventing decode starvation under speculative decoding.
items.body:
## Motivation

With DFlash-family speculative decoding (DFlash, DSpark), the min-free-slots delayer is on by default.
Its threshold comes from `max_running_requests`: `min(4, max(2, (max_running_requests + 5) // 6))`, which is 4 once `max_running_requests >= 19`.
`pp_max_micro_batch_size` (`--pp-max-micro-batch-size`, or `max_running_requests // pp_size` by default) caps the per-step admission budget at `cap - running` (`get_num_allocatable_reqs`).
With a cap of 2-4, the threshold can never be met while any request runs, so every admission waits for the running batch to drain and decode mostly

`WatermarkState.init_from_prompt()` builds the context buffer with `torch.tensor(..., dtype=torch.int32)`. items.author: KrishnanPrash
items.summary: Disables GPU video decoding in the Nemotron VL processor so frames arrive as NumPy arrays for PIL instead of CUDA tensors causing HTTP 500 on all video requests.

## Motivation

Fixes #53177. With default flags, every video request to a Nemotron VL model returns HTTP 500. SGLang decodes video on the GPU by default, so the sampled frames are CUDA tensors, and this processor passes each frame to `PIL.Image.fromarray`, which needs a NumPy array. The processor already turns off GPU decode for images for this reason. This PR turns it off for video too, so frames decode on the CPU and reach PIL as NumPy arrays. No server flag selects CPU decode for this model, so there is no workaround without a code change.

items.title: [Fix] scheduler: respect KV cache page size when deferring requests with a shared prefix
items.author: xiaoxianma
items.summary: The scheduler can intentionally make a request wait when an earlier request is about to compute the same prompt prefix. That saves work only if the later request can reuse the earlier request’s KV cache.
items.body:
## Motivation

The scheduler can intentionally make a request wait when an earlier request is about to compute the same prompt prefix. That saves work only if the later request can reuse the earlier request’s KV cache. The waiting queue compares token IDs, but the GPU KV cache shares states in whole pages. With the default cutoff of 32 tokens and a page size of 64, the scheduler can spot a match that is too short to reuse.

For example, suppose two requests fit in the first prefill batch:

- **A:** 160 prompt tokens.

- **B:** 192 prompt tokens. The first 63 match A, but token 64 differs.

items.title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Use expandable segments under the extensible KV cache's torch memory cap
items.author: AndreasKaratzas
items.summary: Switches PyTorch to expandable segment allocation under ROCm's extensible KV cache memory cap, eliminating allocator fragmentation that caused OOM failures in MTP correctness tests.
items.body:
## Overview

On ROCm, PyTorch now allocates from expandable segments while the extensible KV cache's torch memory cap is set, and goes back to its default segments when the cap is lifted.

Under the cap, PyTorch's default segments can leave more memory reserved but unusable than the cap has room for: one small tensor placed in a cached logits-sized block keeps the rest of that block reserved. That is the cap OOM of `test_mtp_correctness[gemma4-e4b]` on scheduled ROCm builds (https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100488, https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104756, https://buildkite.com/vllm/c

items.body:
## Motivation

The trace level is global (`SGLANG_TRACE_LEVEL` / `/set_trace_level`). Level 3 adds a `decode_loop` slice per decode step, which is hundreds of spans per request, so turning it on for a whole busy server is too heavy for most trace backends. This lets the caller pick the level per request instead, e.g. record 1% of requests at level 3 and the rest at level 1.

- `get_request_trace_level(external_trace_header)` in `srt/observability/trace.py`: returns the level in the caller's `tracestate: sglang=<level>`, otherwise the global level, exactly as before.

items.title: [Feature] Add experimental uniform SPARE for Granite Mamba2
items.author: tbn5pj
items.summary: Adds training-free low-rank recurrent-state compression (SPARE) for Mamba2 models, cutting state memory 4x and boosting decode throughput via existing Triton kernels.
items.body:
## Overview

This PR introduces **SPARE (State Projection for Accelerated Recurrent Execution)**, an experimental, training-free approach to low-rank recurrent-state compression for Mamba2 hybrid language models, initially supporting Granite.

The key idea is to perform recurrent state updates and readouts directly in a low-dimensional space, reducing persistent state memory and memory traffic without reconstructing the original dense state.

SPARE reuses vLLM's native Triton SSD and SSU kernels and existing hybrid cache management. The feature is disabled by default.

Related RFC: #69854

items.title: feat(post-training): expose LSQ minimum LR and weight-decay policy
items.author: asolergi-nv
items.summary: Wires LSQ learned-scale minimum learning rate and weight-decay multiplier through ModelOpt config, CLI, and optimizer setup for quantization training.
items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

Let MLM's ModelOpt training configuration give learned quantization scales their own minimum learning rate and weight-decay multiplier. The shared LSQ helper introduced in #9791 already accepts these settings; this PR wires them through model configuration, CLI, and optimizer setup, and validates them.

items.title: [Perf] dspark: Fuse selected-token logprobs after verification
items.author: jeremyzhang866
items.summary: I noticed this while tracing in DSpark. When a batch only asks for the generated tokens' logprobs, we still build a logprob table for the whole vocabulary and pick one value from each row.
items.body:
Closes #53146.

I noticed this while tracing `return_logprob` in DSpark. When a batch only asks for the generated tokens' logprobs, we still build a logprob table for the whole vocabulary and pick one value from each row. The patch computes the normalizer in tiles and writes just that value. Requests for top logprobs or scores for extra token IDs keep using the existing path.

On one H20, I profiled this step with synthetic FP32 inputs (64 requests × 6 verify positions, vocab 129,280). GPU kernel time went from **626.0 to 96.2 µs**, and extra peak allocation went from **380.00 to 0.19 MiB**.

items.title: [Fix] scheduler: Count all non-idle time in the PD prefill busy counter
items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Fixes PD prefill busy counter to include all non-idle wall time (bootstrap, KV transfer, decode binding) instead of only prefill step time, correcting load-report metrics for scalers.
items.body:
## Motivation

A prefill engine in PD disaggregation publishes `total_prefill_busy_us` and `total_prefill_uncached_tokens` in its load reports (`LoadStat` and `LoadSnapshot`). The router reads their deltas as prefill throughput (uncached tokens per busy second) and, from that, the queue time of the waiting tokens; a busy fraction derived from the same counter is what a scaler of the prefill pool sees.

items.summary: That check came in with #47206, and #66399 moved it to the CPU. The imbalance is max/mean of per-rank load. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Purpose

On ROCm, synchronous EPLB (`use_async: false`) skips a rearrangement when the proposed placement improves the rank load imbalance by less than 5%. That check came in with #47206, and #66399 moved it to the CPU.

The imbalance is max/mean of per-rank load. It is computed on loads summed over the whole load window and over all MoE layers. On real traffic that sum is almost always within a few percent of balanced, because each layer's hot ranks are different and cancel out. So the check skips nearly every rearrangement, and synchronous EPLB on ROCm in practice never moves experts.

## Overview

The CPU `rms_norm` kernel ignores the row dimension of a 2D weight and applies row 0 to every token. ## Overview

Adds an opt-in `share_replicated_regions` kv connector extra config argument to `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`. When this argument is set to `true`, KV regions that are identical on every TP rank, like the MiniMax-M3 index cache, are kept only once in host memory that is shared by all ranks instead of being stored once per rank, so that the same `cpu_bytes_to_use` can hold more blocks.



## Claims

- New argument for `kv_connector_extra_config`, `share_replicated_regions`, for the `cpu` backend under TP on one node. Layers whose spec declares `max_tp_shards=1` are stored by rank 0

## Overview

With `FLEX_ATTENTION`, `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B` kills the engine with `torch._dynamo.exc.FailOnRecompileLimitHit` after a handful of prompt lengths. Its layers hand `FlexAttentionImpl.forward` the query in two memory layouts, and each layout compiles its own set of `flex_attention` graphs. This makes the decoder query contiguous before it is permuted for the compiled call.

## Overview

Allow `--prefix-match-unit` to be smaller than `--block-size` for models with a single full-attention KV cache group. Such a config now uses the copy-on-write partial-hit path that hybrid models already have, so requests sharing a prompt that ends inside a block hit the prompt tail instead of recomputing it. This addresses the n>1 regression in #69408, caused by the default block size moving from 16 to 64 (#63231), without giving up 64-token blocks.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] gfx1100: use wvSplitK for decode GEMMs with 6-8 rows
items.author: Shan2L
items.summary: On gfx1100 (RDNA3), decode steps with 6-8 tokens run their unquantized linear layers through hipBLASLt, because sends only 1-5 rows to the skinny kernel. For these shapes hipBLASLt picks small tiles that run at 1.10-1.24x of the DRAM-bandwidth floor, while sta…
items.body:
## Overview

On gfx1100 (RDNA3), decode steps with 6-8 tokens run their unquantized linear layers through hipBLASLt, because `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` sends only 1-5 rows to the skinny `wvSplitK` kernel. For these shapes hipBLASLt picks small tiles that run at 1.10-1.24x of the DRAM-bandwidth floor, while `wvSplitK` stays at 1.04-1.15x. This PR extends `wvSplitK` to 6-8 rows on gfx1100.

It stops at 8 rows on purpose: at 12 rows `wvSplitK` only ties hipBLASLt, and at 16 rows it is slower on every Qwen3.5-9B shape except the lm_head. A 6-16 version made batch-16 decode 10% slower end to end

items.title: [Fix] bench: Count tokens, not chunks, in peak output throughput
items.author: decajoin
items.summary: In, computes ("Peak output token throughput") by adding per timestamp in. Because streaming endpoints record one entry per SSE chunk—and a single chunk can bundle multiple tokens (e.g., under speculative decoding), while non-streaming requests produce only a s…
items.body:
## Motivation

In `python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py`, `calculate_metrics()` computes `max_output_tokens_per_s` ("Peak output token throughput") by adding `1` per timestamp in `[ttft, *itl]`.

Because streaming endpoints record one `itl` entry per SSE chunk—and a single chunk can bundle multiple tokens (e.g., under speculative decoding), while non-streaming requests produce only a single timestamp—this counts **chunks/s rather than tokens/s**. Under speculative decoding, the reported peak output throughput can fall well below the average `output_throughput` (which uses `output.output_len`).

## Motivation

Internal rollout serving is created as a named, detached Ray actor (`ServingCluster`, with `RolloutManager` alongside) so that a failed or interrupted run can be restarted and reattach to the same engines. `RolloutStartup.close(failed=True)` therefore only detaches the trainers; engines, routers and their GPU placement groups stay alive until a later driver reuses or disposes them. Only a successful run disposes them. There is currently no option to change this.

For LongRoPE checkpoints (128k Phi-3/Phi-3.5, Phi-4-mini) the PyTorch backend builds one RoPE table at load. items.title: [fsdp] fix: use actual chunk count for TiledMLP last-shard gradient write-back
items.author: four1er
items.summary: Fixes #8839 dropped parameter gradients accumulated by earlier micro-batches whenever returned fewer chunks than (e.g. moves any existing into its buffer and writes it back only from the hook installed with, and never fired in that case, so the accumulated gra…
items.body:
Fixes #8839

`TiledMLP.backward` dropped parameter gradients accumulated by earlier micro-batches whenever `torch.chunk` returned fewer chunks than `num_shards` (e.g. `n=9, shards=4` gives 3 chunks of 3). `GradientAccumulator` moves any existing `param.grad` into its buffer and writes it back only from the hook installed with `is_last_shard=True`, and `is_last_shard = i + 1 == shards` never fired in that case, so the accumulated gradients were silently lost.

This PR uses the actual chunk count (`len(x_shards)`) for the last-shard test, so the write-back hook always fires on the final shard.

items.author: tianyi-zhang-02
items.summary: A hybrid model can reuse a cached prefix only if the recurrent (Mamba) state at its end is still in SGLang's fixed-size state pool, which is evicted by LRU. With many prompts in flight, the prompts' states are the oldest and go first, so later samples of the s…
items.body:
### Feature request

For hybrid models (Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Next) on the SGLang rollout, hold each prompt's prefix state with an SGLang session (`--enable-session-radix-cache`, sglang >= 0.5.17, sgl-project/sglang#29173) until all samples of that prompt are done, then close the session.

### Motivation

A hybrid model can reuse a cached prefix only if the recurrent (Mamba) state at its end is still in SGLang's fixed-size state pool, which is evicted by LRU. With many prompts in flight, the prompts' states are the oldest and go first, so later samples of the same prompt recompute the whole prompt.

items.author: Hang-get
items.summary: Ray workers set, but the DeepEP buffer wrappers still build their communicator from an MPI split. DeepEP's buffer constructor uses that communicator's rank count, so the low-latency strategy can initialize a one-rank buffer for a multi-rank EP mapping.
items.body:
## Description

Ray workers set `TLLM_DISABLE_MPI=1`, but the DeepEP buffer wrappers still build their communicator from an MPI split. DeepEP's buffer constructor uses that communicator's rank count, so the low-latency strategy can initialize a one-rank buffer for a multi-rank EP mapping. Normal DeepEP is usually rejected earlier by its local-MPI feasibility check.

items.body:
## Description

trtllm-bench's async client dispatches its whole inbox into request tasks when the benchmark starts. For the rest of the run, `LlmManager.worker` then polled the empty inbox with `await asyncio.sleep(0)`, so the event loop never blocked: the client process kept a core busy and held the GIL most of the time. The LLM API thread that delivers each response to the request coroutines needs the GIL too.

On two-socket Intel hosts with Linux 5.15, like QA's H100 nodes, this starves that thread. CPython restarts a waiting thread's 5 ms switch timeout every time the GIL holder releases

items.title: [V1 FSDP] update_weights broadcasts full params every step (~9s/step on 32B); no delta or bucketed sync mode
items.author: dahai80
items.summary: On the V1 FSDP path, (actor → rollout engine weight sync) broadcasts the full parameter set every training step. Measured cost on Qwen2.5-32B TP8: ~9 s/step, every step, regardless of how few parameters changed.
items.body:
## Summary

On the V1 FSDP path, `update_weights` (actor → rollout engine weight sync) broadcasts the **full parameter set every training step**. Measured cost on Qwen2.5-32B TP8: ~9 s/step, every step, regardless of how few parameters changed. Over hundreds of GRPO steps this is a fixed tax proportional to model size, not to actual weight drift.

## Suggestion

A bucketed delta mode would remove most of this cost:

- hash/checksum per parameter bucket, sync only buckets whose checksum changed (in practice almost none change every step in RL fine-tuning — the update is small relative to init)

items.body:
## Purpose

Implement the existing `--check-weight-update-equal` flag for the first actor-to-rollout weight update. Before the first rollout, Vime verifies that the trainer can restore the target-model parameters originally loaded by each vLLM endpoint. This check assumes that the trainer and rollout engines start from the same logical checkpoint.

Resetting the parameters before the update makes a missed transfer observable: if an update skips a previously nonzero tensor, its digest will differ from the saved baseline. See [RFC #537](https://github.com/vllm-project/vime/issues/537).

The NVLS AllGather-V and ReduceScatter-V kernels, and the ordered ReduceScatter-V used by batch-invariant mode, returned before their barrier when a CTA's `pid >= ep_max_tokens`. items.author: Doublrest
items.summary: In V1 trainers ( and ), whitens advantages once over the full sampled batch, whereas splits the batch into optimizer chunks without re-normalizing per chunk. When the sampled batch is larger than, individual optimizer chunks can have non-zero token-weighted ad…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8766.

In V1 trainers (`sync` and `colocate_async`), `_compute_advantage()` whitens advantages once over the full sampled batch, whereas `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()` splits the batch into `ppo_mini_batch_size` optimizer chunks without re-normalizing per chunk. When the sampled batch is larger than `ppo_mini_batch_size`, individual optimizer chunks can have non-zero token-weighted advantage means, introducing chunk-level policy-gradient drift.

This PR re-normalizes `mini_batch_td["advantages"]` per optimizer chunk in `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()`

items.author: AmineDiro
items.summary: On verl v0.9.1, verl's own Qwen2-7B-Instruct GRPO GSM8K recipe (the baseline in ) crashed twice on 8x B200, both times on the first training step after a validation pass. Right before the crash, the agent-loop workers log and carry on.
items.body:
## Summary

On verl v0.9.1, verl's own Qwen2-7B-Instruct GRPO GSM8K recipe (the `qwen2-7b-fsdp2.log` baseline in `docs/algo/baseline.md`) crashed twice on 8x B200, both times on the first training step after a validation pass. Right before the crash, the agent-loop workers log `Timeout waiting for data status update ACK from controller after 30s` and carry on. The data was written to storage but the controller never marks it ready, so the trainer later gets an empty batch from TransferQueue and fails with `KeyError: 'loss_mask'` in `compute_log_prob`.

The timeout itself is a slow controller.

items.title: Retire engines that died during training before the weight update
items.author: GaokaiZhang
items.summary: An engine that dies in that window stays registered in the router and in the engine list. The next sends it, the request fails with, and the run stops.
items.body:
## Problem

The health monitors are paused from the end of a rollout (`finish_rollout`) to the weight update. An engine that dies in that window stays registered in the router and in the engine list. The next `update_weights` sends it `pause_generation`, the request fails with `ConnectionRefusedError`, and the run stops. With the fully-async rollout the periodic check does not help either: each resume restarts the first wait (600 s by default), so no periodic check runs when a rollout takes less than that. items.title: [algo, trainer, fsdp, megatron, cfg, doc] feat: add topk_rb KL loss (top-k Rao-Blackwellised KL to the reference)
items.author: hiddevandebeek
items.summary: It adds, a KL penalty against the reference policy for. The estimator computes KL(πθ ‖ πref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Implements the RFC in #8536. It adds `actor.kl_loss_type: topk_rb`, a KL penalty against the reference policy for `use_kl_loss=True`.

The estimator computes KL(π_θ ‖ π_ref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket. The within-tail part is estimated from the sampled token, so the result is an **unbiased** estimate of the full-vocabulary KL gradient at every k, with much lower variance than the single-sample `kl`/`k2`/`low_var_kl`/`k3+` options. It is the per-token Rao-Blackwellised KL of [Amini et al., NeurIPS 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.1063

### What does this PR do?

Preserve vLLM's `finish_reason="length"` in `TokenOutput.stop_reason`. Today the vLLM rollout server reports `completed` both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends `end_turn` for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work still in progress.

### Design and compatibility

Map vLLM's `stop` to `completed` and let `length` pass through the existing fallback. Callers can now return `max_tokens` to Anthropic clients. Abort still maps to `aborted`

items.title: [reward] fix: compare prime_code call-based outputs as plain builtins
items.author: Aarav500
items.summary: In, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of or whose always returns got full reward on every call-based task.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8656. In `prime_code`, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with `output == expected`. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of `int` or `list` whose `__eq__` always returns `True` got full reward on every call-based task. Swapping the operands doesn't help, because Python tries a subclass's reflected `__eq__` first.

This adds `_to_builtin()` in `prime_code/testing_util.py` and applies it to the output right after the existing `json.dumps(output)` call. It rebuilds the value from plain `None`/`bool`/`int`/`float

## Motivation

`Float16Module.forward` upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with `labels=None`, so the whole `[T, V]` logits tensor is copied to fp32. It is the largest single allocation in a long-context actor step: 40,960 tokens × 248,320 vocabulary is about 41 GB in fp32 versus 20 GB in bf16.

items.title: [Test][Ascend] Validate Qwen3-0.6B disk delta updates against full checkpoint
items.author: wangx700
items.summary: Strengthen the Qwen3-0.6B disk-delta test with an independent full-checkpoint and inference comparison. Run two real training/update rounds for both XOR and overwrite.
items.body:
Strengthen the Qwen3-0.6B disk-delta test with an independent full-checkpoint and inference comparison.

Test flow:
1. Run two real training/update rounds for both XOR and overwrite.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Those paths expect, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.
items.body:
## Background

A custom generation function may return multiple training segments for one input. `generate_and_rm_group` preserves that result as `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.
- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.
- Preserve the original nested return shape for d

items.title: fix(rollout): handle nested aborted fully-async results
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.
items.body:
## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.author: shaurya416
items.summary: Fixes #2409 ## Problem falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply.
items.body:
Fixes #2409

## Problem

`compute_gpqa_reward` falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply. A reply that never answers, for example `I'm sorry, but I can't help with that.`, therefore scored 1.0 whenever the gold letter (`a`, `b`, `c`) occurred inside a word, and a short numeric choice such as `11` matched inside `2011` or `111`.

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

items.author: tengeel

items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

items.title: [Bugfix][Training] Preserve DSpark rotary embedding dtype
items.author: LOGO127
items.summary: Fix DSpark rotary tables being cast to integer position-ID dtype, and preserve FP32 phases after parent-module dtype conversions and under autocast. Original PR commit:.
items.body:
## Summary

Fix DSpark rotary tables being cast to integer position-ID dtype, and preserve FP32 phases after parent-module dtype conversions and under autocast.

- Keep cosine/sine floating point; convert them to the query dtype only at the attention boundary.
- Recompute inverse frequencies directly in FP32 on the positions device instead of widening an already-rounded FP16/BF16 buffer.

items.body:
## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

## Summary

`_parse_extra_env_vars` split each assignment on every `=` and then kept only the second component. For example:

was parsed as:

In the agentic rollout path, each agent turn sends a request to SGLang through the SGLang router. When a request is cancelled or hits the client-side read timeout, Slime must explicitly abort the corresponding SGLang request to release its scheduler slot and KV-cache resources.

items.body:
## Problem

In non-colocated full NCCL weight updates with pipeline-parallel training and multiple independent SGLang rollout engines, each PP source creates a custom `slime-pp_<rank>` group containing itself and every engine GPU.

The PP sources are Ray actors invoked concurrently. Each rollout-engine actor uses a blocking HTTP call to join a group and processes methods serially. If engine 0 starts PP0 while engine 1 starts PP1, each group waits for the request queued behind the other engine's blocking call. ## Summary

Long full-history prompt rendering blocks the agent adapter's aiohttp event loop. Move the existing `_session_prompt_ids()` call to one adapter-owned worker thread, retaining exact upstream rendering, saved sampled-token prefixes, and safe fallback for changed histories/tool schemas.
